question: Should OpenClaw accept a core Claw mission-control runtime/config surface now, or pause this branch until a maintainer-sponsored SQLite, security-boundary, and real-proof design is ready?
rationale: The branch is a broad new product/runtime surface with storage, security, session-state, and configuration implications that cannot be accepted as a routine external feature PR.

options.title: Pause for sponsored rewrite
options.body: Keep this work out of merge flow until maintainers sponsor the product/API shape and the branch is rebuilt around SQLite state, path containment, SSRF helper preservation, and real proof.

options.title: Repair before merge
options.body: Ask the contributor or an adopted repair branch to address the blocking storage, path, and SSRF defects plus add real behavior proof before another merge-readiness review.

options.title: Accept experimental risk
options.body: Maintainers could explicitly accept the broad experimental surface, but current evidence leaves security and state risks unresolved.

recommendation.title: Pause for sponsored rewrite
recommendation.body: Keep this work out of merge flow until maintainers sponsor the product/API shape and the branch is rebuilt around SQLite state, path containment, SSRF helper preservation, and real proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product-direction choice for a broad new core runtime surface, with Vincent Koc as the likely technical reviewer for the Gateway/state/security details.
